questions.stem: What is the zona orbicularis related to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Zona orbicularis is related to the neck of femur. They are the circular fibers of the capsule of hip joint.

Capsule of the hip joint is made up of 2 sets of fibers: 

  • Circular fibers or zona orbicularis - They are internal and form a collar around the neck of femur. They are blended with the pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments
  • Longitudinal fibers - They are external. These fibers are numerous in the anterosuperior region and are joined by iliofemoral ligament.

The image given below shows the zona orbicularis.






Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1377

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false about the ligaments of the hip joint?

options.label: A
options.text: Iliofemoral ligament is the strongest ligament of hip joint

options.label: B
options.text: Transverse acetabular ligament contains cartilage cells

options.label: C
options.text: Ischiofemoral fibers fuse with the zona orbicularis

options.label: D
options.text: Pubofemoral ligament is triangular in shape

questions.answerText: Transverse acetabular ligament contains cartilage cells
questions.solutionHtml:
Transverse acetabular ligament does not contain cartilage cells. This ligament crosses the acetabular notch and continues peripherally with the labrum. 

Ligaments of the hip joint are:

  1. Iliofemoral ligament - strongest ligament of hip joint
  2. Pubofemoral ligament - triangular in shape
  3. Ischiofemoral ligament - some fibers fuse with zona orbicularis and inferior fibers attach to the posterior circumference of femoral neck
  4. Transverse acetabular ligament - forms a foramen to allow vessels and nerves to enter the hip joint
  5. Ligament of head of femur - apex is attached to fovea and base is attached to the edges of acetabular notch

The images given below show the ligaments of the hip joint.



Note: Iliocapsularis is a muscle that lies immediately deep to the tendon of iliopsoas and above the anterior hip capsule. The function of the muscle is not clear and is thought to taut the hip capsule to prevent its impingement during the hip flexion.








Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page 1378

questions.stem: A 16-year-old gymnast was brought to the emergency department after suffering severe trauma during the performance. She presented with painful hip instability. MRI revealed ligament tear which is caused by hyperextension of the hip joint. Which of the following​ ligaments is likely to be torn?
questions.solutionHtml:
The iliofemoral ligament resists the hyperextension of hip joint and hence, is likely to be injured.

Iliofemoral ligament or ligament of Bigelow is the strongest ligament of the hip joint. It is an inverted-Y-shaped ligament. The apex is attached between the anterior inferior iliac spine and acetabular margin. The base is attached to the intertrochanteric line. This ligament prevents the hyperextension of the hip joint.

The image given below shows the iliofemoral ligament.






Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page nos 1378 and 1379

questions.stem: A 30-year-old male presented with pain and stiffness of the right hip. Ultrasonography revealed effusion in the right hip joint. At which position of hip joint will the pain be minimal?
questions.solutionHtml:
A patient with an effusion in the hip joint is has least pain in flexed and abducted position.

Joint capacity is maximal when the hip joint is held in a partially flexed and abducted position. Hence, a patient with an effusion in the hip joint is therefore most comfortable in this position. 





Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1378

questions.stemHtml: Artery passing through the structure marked in the diagram below is a branch of:
questions.solutionHtml:
The image shown is the ligament of head of the femur and the artery passing through it is the foveal artery/ artery of ligament of head of femur. It is derived from the acetabular branch of obturator artery.

The blood supply of the femoral head is derived from an arterial ring (trochanteric anastomosis) around the neck of femur constituted by:

  • Medial circumflex femoral arteries 
  • Lateral circumflex femoral arteries
  • Superior and inferior gluteal vessels (minor contributions)





Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1378, Fig 81.7

questions.stemHtml: Identify the structures attached to the areas marked 1, 5, and 6 in the tibial plateau below?

options.label: A
options.text: Anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, anterior and posterior horns of medial meniscus

options.label: B
options.text: Anterior horn of medial meniscus, posterior horn of medial meniscus, anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments

options.label: C
options.text: Anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, anterior and posterior horns of lateral meniscus

options.label: D
options.text: Anterior horn of lateral meniscus, posterior horn of lateral meniscus, anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments

questions.answerText: Anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, anterior and posterior horns of medial meniscus
questions.solutionHtml:
The structures attached to the areas marked 1, 5, and 6 in the tibial plateau are anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, anterior and posterior horns of medial meniscus respectively.



Remember the attachments of ligaments from anterior to posterior as:

Mnemonic: Medical College Ludhiana Ludhiana Medical College

  • M: Medial meniscus (Anterior horn)
  • C: Cruciate ligament (Anterior)
  • L: Lateral meniscus (Anterior horn)
  • L: Lateral meniscus (Posterior horn)
  • M: Medial meniscus (Posterior horn)
  • C: Cruciate ligament (Posterior)





Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1387

questions.stem: A 19-year-old football player was brought to the hospital after he suffered an ​injury caused by a lateral blow to the knee joint. MRI revealed an injury to the ligaments commonly referred to as the 'unhappy triad'. Which of the following ligaments are involved?

options.label: B
options.text: Posterior cruciate ligament and lateral meniscus

options.label: C
options.text: Anterior cruciate ligament and medial meniscus

options.label: D
options.text: Anterior and posterior horns of lateral meniscus

questions.answerText: Anterior cruciate ligament and medial meniscus
questions.solutionHtml:
The unhappy triad of the knee involves:

  • Medial meniscus
  • Anterior cruciate ligament
  • Tibial collateral ligament

questions.stem: A 35-year-old basketball player with knee pain was diagnosed to have coronary ligament strain. Which of the following ligaments is involved?
questions.solutionHtml:
Coronary ligaments are also known as meniscotibial ligaments. It refers to the tibial attachment of medial meniscus.

The medial meniscus is almost a semicircle in shape. It is attached by its anterior horn to the anterior tibial intercondylar area in front of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior horn is fixed to the posterior tibial intercondylar area, between the attachments of the lateral meniscus and posterior cruciate ligament.

These attachments ensure that the medial meniscus is relatively fixed and moves much less than the lateral meniscus.

The image given below shows the cranial and caudal meniscotibial ligament.






Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1388

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false?

options.label: A
options.text: Lateral meniscus covers a larger area of the articular surface than medial meniscus

options.label: B
options.text: Movements of lateral meniscus is restricted compared to medial meniscus

options.label: C
options.text: Peripheral tears of the menisci heal better than central tears

options.label: D
options.text: Suprapatellar bursa is an extension of knee joint cavity

questions.answerText: Movements of lateral meniscus is restricted compared to medial meniscus
questions.solutionHtml:
The movements of medial meniscus are restricted compared to the lateral meniscus

Comparison between medial and lateral menisci:

Feature Lateral meniscus Medial meniscus

Mobility

More mobile

 Relatively fixed and therefore moves much less than lateral meniscus
Shape Forms approximately 4/5th of a circle Semicircular in shape
Area covered Covers a larger area Covers less area than lateral meniscus

Additional 

features

 Grooved posterolaterally by Popliteus tendon, which separates it from fibular collateral ligament -

Option C: Peripheral zone of menisci are vascularized by capillary loops and inner regions are less vascular. Hence, relative healing rate is better in peripheral zone.

Option D: Suprapatellar bursa is the superior extension of the knee joint cavity. It lies between the femur and suprapatellar part of quadriceps femoris.





Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page nos 1388-91

questions.stem: Which of the following is involved in locking of knee?

options.label: A
options.text: Lateral rotation of the femur on tibia during extension

options.label: B
options.text: Medial rotation of the femur on tibia during flexion

options.label: C
options.text: Lateral rotation of the femur on tibia during flexion

options.label: D
options.text: Medial rotation of the femur on tibia during extension

questions.answerText: Medial rotation of the femur on tibia during extension
questions.solutionHtml:
Locking of knee is medial rotation of femur on tibia during the later stages of extension.

When standing, the knee joint is locked into position to reduce the amount of muscle work needed to maintain the standing position. The muscle responsible for locking is vastus medialis.

The image given below shows the locking of knee joint on standing.



Unlocking of the knee joint is the lateral rotation of femur on tibia during the beginning of flexion. This is brought by the action of popliteus muscle.






Gray's Anatomy for Students: 3rd Edition, Page nos 612 and 13
Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1392

questions.stem: Which bursae are involved in patients with clergyman's knee and housemaid's knee?

options.label: A
options.text: Prepatellar bursa and infrapatellar bursa respectively

options.label: B
options.text: Subcutaneous and deep infrapatellar bursa respectively

options.label: C
options.text: Infrapatellar bursa and prepatellar bursa respectively

questions.answerText: Infrapatellar bursa and prepatellar bursa respectively
questions.solutionHtml:
Clergyman's knee and housemaid's knee results from inflammation of infrapatellar bursa and prepatellar bursa respectively.

Lower limb major bursitis:

  • Prepatellar Bursitis (Housemaid's Knee)
  • Infrapatellar bursitis (Clergyman's knee) 
  • Trochanteric Bursitis (Above hip abductor) 

The image shows a sagittal section through the left knee joint (lateral aspect) with bursae.






Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1392

questions.stem: A 23-year-old cricketer was diagnosed with ligamentum mucosum tear. Range of movements of which of the following joints is affected?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ligamentum mucosum is related to the knee joint. It is a plica present at the intercondylar notch of the knee joint.

Plicae are the embryological remnants of synovial folds. Major plicae around knee joint are:

  • Ligamentum mucosum - intercondylar notch
  • Suprapatellar plica - suprapatellar space
  • Medial plica - extending from infrapatellar fat pad to medial wall of knee

Plica syndrome is a painful knee function due to thickened and inflamed synovial folds. It most commonly involves the medial plica.

The image given below shows the synovial plicae.






Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1391

questions.stem: A patient presented to the orthopedics​ OPD with ankle sprain caused due to hyper inversion of the right foot. Which of the following ligaments is commonly injured?
questions.solutionHtml:
The anterior talofibular ligament is most commonly injured with inversion sprains.

Important ligaments of ankle present on the lateral side, and therefore likely to be injured in inversion sprains include:

  • Anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) - most commonly injured
  • Posterior talofibular ligament (PTFL)
  • Calcaneofibular ligament (CFL)

The image given below shows the ligaments attached to the lateral side of ankle.



Important ligaments of ankle present on the medial side, and therefore likely to be injured in eversion sprains include:

  • Deltoid ligament (Medial collateral ligament)
  • Spring ligament (calcaneonavicular ligament)

The image given below shows the ligaments attached to the medial side of ankle.







Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1431
Gray's anatomy: The anatomical basis of clinical practice - 42nd edition, Page no 1445

questions.stem: The superficial part of deltoid ligament is attached to all of the following except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Superficial part of deltoid ligament is attached to all bones except fibula.

Deltoid ligament or medial collateral ligament is a strong triangular band, attached to the apex, the anterior and posterior borders of the medial malleolus. It has 2 layers, superficial and deep:

  • Superficial layer consists of tibionavicular fibers anteriorly, tibiocalcaneal fibers in the middle, and superficial posterior tibiotalar fibers posteriorly.
  • Deep layer consists of anterior tibiotalar fibres, tibiocalcaneal in the middle and deep posterior tibiotalar posteriorly.





Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1431
Gray's anatomy: The anatomical basis of clinical practice - 42nd edition, Page no 1445

questions.stemHtml: Which ligament is related to the inferior surface of the structure marked in the image?
questions.solutionHtml:
The structure marked in the image is the head of talus. The ligament related to its inferior surface is the spring ligament/ calcaneonavicular ligament.

The inferior surface of the head of talus has three facets:

  • Posterior facet - It is the largest facet and articulates with the sustentaculum tali of the calcaneus.
  • Anterolateral facet - It articulates with the anterior facet of the calcaneus.
  • Medial facet - It is related to the spring ligament.




Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1423

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following statements is false regarding the structure marked in the image?

options.label: A
options.text: It has a triangular fibrocartilaginous facet on which part of the talar head rests

options.label: B
options.text: Transection of the ligament leads to adult acquired flat foot

options.label: C
options.text: It is a complex of two ligaments

options.label: D
options.text: It maintains the medial longitudinal arch of foot

questions.answerText: It is a complex of two ligaments
questions.solutionHtml:
In the given image, the structure marked is the spring ligament (plantar calcaneo-navicular ligament). It is a complex of three ligaments, namely:

  • Superomedial calcaneonavicular ligament
  • Medioplantar oblique calcaneonavicular ligament
  • Inferoplantar longitudinal calcaneonavicular ligament

The spring ligament is a thick band connecting the anterior margin of the sustentaculum tali to the plantar surface of the navicular.

It is the stabilizer of medial longitudinal arch and the head of the talus. Disruption of this ligament leads to the collapse of medial longitudinal arch and causes flat foot.

The image given below shows the spring ligament.






Online Resource, Spring ligament complex: Illustrated normal anatomy and spectrum of ... https://www.ejradiology.com/article/S0720-048X(16)30292-3/abstract
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/27077591
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/27776669

Lisfranc's ligament is cuneometatarsal interosseous ligament.

There are three cuneometatarsal interosseous ligaments and the strongest ligament is Lisfranc's ligament. It passes from the lateral surface of the medial cuneiform to the adjacent angle of the second metatarsal bone. Deformity of this ligament can lead to instability and deformity of tarsometatarsal joint.






Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1437

questions.stem: Chopart's ligament is related to which of the following joints?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chopart's ligament is related to both calcaneocuboid and calcaneonavicular joints.

Chopart's ligament/ Bifurcate ligament is a strong Y- shaped band, having a proximal stem and 2 distal limbs.

  • The proximal limb is attached by a stem to the anterior part of upper calcaneal surface.
  • The distal limb divides into calcaneocuboid and calcaneonavicular parts.

The image given below shows the Chopart's ligament.






Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no 1436
